root_causes.description: product-catalog sits on the sole shared downstream path of the user-facing frontend (and of checkout and recommendation per topology). Its degraded request handling pins the server-span p99 of every caller to a hard 10s ceiling, surfacing as a sustained 10s p99 latency at the frontend, coupled with a ~90x CPU anomaly on the catalog pods.

evidence.observed_value: p99=10000.000 ms sustained (mean=p50=p95=p99=max=10000ms), a flat 10s ceiling
evidence.expected_baseline: frontend p99 < ~100 ms in normal operation
error_rate < 0.01 — confirms a latency, not error, fault

root_causes.description: product-catalog is the only component with a resource anomaly: its container CPU is ~90x that of peers (1.93 cores vs 0.021). If the injected fault is CPU saturation (StressChaos) rather than a pure latency injection, the CPU contention would slow request handling and inflate caller latency.

evidence.observed_value: p99=10000.000 ms (10s ceiling) at the frontend caller

root_causes.description: frontend exhibits the user-visible 10s p99 latency, but topology shows it is purely a caller of product-catalog (also checkout/recommendation/cart/shipping/currency/ad) and it has no resource anomaly of its own, so the latency is a propagated symptom rather than the origin.

remediation_steps: Inspect product-catalog pods for injected chaos (latency/stress) — check pod annotations and events, and run `kubectl top pod -n otel-demo` to confirm the ~1.9-core CPU burn; remove the fault once identified.

Verify product-catalog resource requests/limits and CPU throttling; raise limits or scale replicas if the saturation is organic, since catalog is the shared hot path for frontend, checkout and recommendation.
Validate recovery by re-checking frontend server-span p99 returns from the 10s ceiling to <100ms and product-catalog CPU drops back toward ~0.02 cores.
